answer: Each mining seat is bound to a unique IPv6 /56 prefix lease costing 90 POA per epoch. Five randomly chosen beacons ask the lessee to serve a 12 MB blob derived from H(epoch-seed || prefix) within eight seconds; a timeout, or a second key announcing the same prefix, burns 45 POA and folds both into one seat. A farm that parks a knoll of names behind one uplink therefore buys no extra weight. After two missed probes the lease loses emission, and leftover collateral refunds only after four epochs under a public walnut escrow id. A fresh prefix is required to climb back to the emission zenith.
